commenti.body:
Personally, I think you are reading too much into it.

A24 is a business, one the peddles artistic films, but still one that wants to make money.

So even though some of the themes of First Reformed push against over consumption, I don't think selling a souvenir of the film negates it's message. 

In all honestly, I think the film is much more a reflection on the personal struggles of a priest losing faith in the modern world riddled with consumerism, indifference and climate change.

I think the overconsumption is simply a piece to that puzzle. One that selling a hat from the film does not negate
Yeah, thanks for that. Lost the forest for the trees on that one.
No worries! Its one of my favorite films of the past few years, so any excuse to think about it again is a welcome retreat.

This is a tangent, but I think it's related.  The message(s) of the movie could also be related to longstanding concerns over consumption, but also the frivolities of the fallen world, the market, etc.   Sumptuary laws have a *long* history, and are rooted in how corrupting consumption is through to be.  

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumptuary_law


There are *many* renditions in art of the temptations of St. Anthony, St Jerome, St Francis, etc.  The lures of luxury, empty amusement, the flesh, and other secular pursuits have always been seen to be threats to the spiritual life.   This movie may frame those in environmental terms, but the church has *always* found the market and the 'fallen' world to be dangerous.  Hence another prevalent theme in religious art, memento mori, a reminder that life is fleeting, so we should shun luxury and frivolity, and turn back to the true life of the church.

> it feels so thoughtless that this was even made? Is my disgust justified or am I just too up my own ass here?

I think you're justified to think this, but A24 is not some moral arbiter in the film industry (even though some of its most diehard fans may think it is). They make merchandising decisions in the name of profit just as any other business entity within capitalism will do. Cheaply made, imported, branded merchandise has an immense profit margin - and so on. I can't imagine a fan of the film purchasing that merchandise though - pretty odd behavior, even if they were doing so in an 'ironic' way.
